notes: NO humanoid walking legs or new feet. prompt: Draw the entire two-direction animation sheet for existing game creature MON-020-0 from these two identity references. Image 1 is its canonical FRONT at rest, image 2 is its old approximate rear and may be misleading. Preserve the exact anatomy and colors in image 1. NO humanoid walking legs or new feet. Preserve ALL the original curled pale lower appendages, including the THREE prominent visible curled supports, the original tall angular pale front plates, reddish seams/openings and paired rigid dark ribbed/blocklike side structures. Keep the original silhouette and existing appendage count from front identity reference rather than adding limbs from a generic quad label. The base creeps by restrained traveling curl contractions, with stable upper-body height and mass. Do not bend the rigid upper plates or side structures, add a book, weapon, head, human arms, new tentacles, worm mouth or upright coil copied from the other reference. Correct directional anatomy where necessary. Use fixed slightly elevated square-grid camera. EXACTLY FOUR columns and FOUR rows of equal cells, sixteen complete figures. FIRST TWO ROWS: eight poses all walking TOWARD the camera, down the screen. LAST TWO ROWS: eight poses all traveling AWAY, up the screen, viewed from behind. The rear must show true back or tail, not face, chest, or a flipped front. Preserve equipment on the same anatomical side and respect occlusion. Each two-row block is a short continuous cycle: first row support A, load A, swing B, settle B; second row support B, load B, swing A, settle A. For no-leg creatures interpret these as alternating travel phases of their original body. Keep the same scale, silhouette and head position, small grounded motion where appropriate. All 16 separate figures are drawn whole, centered and fully inside their respective cells, with generous gutters and outside margins. No text, lines, ground, shadows, white matte, glow or particles. Genuine transparent alpha outside every silhouette. Dark matte pixel clusters and original materials.
